Prove all three substantive claims independently, then assemble the conjunction and the `Iff`.

- For surjectivity of `Nat.primeCounting`, use the enumeration of primes: the \(k\)-th prime (with the appropriate indexing convention) has exactly \(k\) primes at or below it. Thus each \(k\) has a witness obtained from `Nat.nth`/the corresponding prime-counting theorem.

- For the forward side of the `Iff`, view twisting by \(\chi\) as multiplication of the \(n\)-th L-series term by a bounded scalar. A Dirichlet character satisfies \(\|\chi(n)\|\le 1\), so
  \[
  \left\|\frac{\chi(n)f(n)}{n^s}\right\|
  \le
  \left\|\frac{f(n)}{n^s}\right\|.
  \]
  Apply the summability comparison principle.

- For the Chebyshev identity, unfold or invoke the defining finite-sum formula
  \[
  \psi(x)=\sum_{n\le \lfloor x\rfloor}\Lambda(n).
  \]
  Rewrite the bounded condition as the finset interval `Finset.Icc 0 (Nat.floor x)`; the endpoint \(0\) causes no issue because the von Mangoldt function vanishes there.

Since both sides of the `Iff` are established outright, obtain the equivalence by pairing the two constant implications rather than seeking a mathematical connection between them.
